GLOWpipeline: Multi-Region Orchestration for GLOW Variant-Set Scans

Overview

GLOWpipeline is the orchestration-and-summary layer of the GLOW software family. It scales the single-region GLOW variant-set test (GLOWr) up to a genome-wide scan: it splits a genome into chunks for a compute-cluster array, runs the GLOWr single-region test over each chunk’s regions under an output policy, and aggregates the per-chunk results into a genome-wide table with significance thresholding and overlapping-window locus merging.

GLOWpipeline is the STAARpipeline analog in the GLOWpipeline -> GLOWr -> GFisher stack. It is deliberately cohort- and cluster-agnostic (resolved objects in, tables out), so a workflow script binds it to a specific dataset and scheduler.

Key Features

  • Genome chunking for cluster arrays: define_genome_chunks() splits a chromosome set into contiguous sliding-window chunks, one chunk per array task, with a no-duplicate / no-gap boundary rule.
  • Single-chunk scan engine: glow_scan_chunk() runs the GLOWr single-region test (GLOWr::glow_region_test()) over a chunk’s windows under a glow_output_policy(), returning a flat per-window results table.
  • Scan-unit runner: run_scan_unit() builds a unit’s regions and filters (build_scan_regions()), runs the per-window scan, and persists the results.
  • Run preparation: prepare_scan_run() resolves the shared setup of a multi-region run (null model, weight inputs, output directories) once, so each chunk task reuses it.
  • Genome-wide aggregation: aggregate_scan_results() concatenates per-chunk window results into a genome-wide table, flags significant windows, and merges overlapping significant windows into loci; aggregate_coding_results() does the gene-centric coding-scan analog.
  • Diagnostics and summaries: per-test genomic-control lambda and QQ plots (summarize_qq_and_lambdas()), completeness checking (check_scan_completeness()), run-log parsing (parse_chr_log(), parse_chunk_log()), and error drill-downs (write_error_drilldowns()).
  • Built on GLOWr (and GFisher): the per-region statistics come from GLOWr, which in turn uses GFisher for the generalized Fisher-type combination p-values.

Installation

From GitHub (recommended) 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/GLOWpipeline")

GLOWpipeline depends on GLOWr (ZWuLab/GLOWr), which itself depends on GFisher (ZWuLab/GFisher). The GitHub install resolves this transitive chain automatically via the Remotes: field in DESCRIPTION; no separate step is needed. For a from-source install you may prefer to install the dependencies first, GFisher before GLOWr:

remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/GFisher")
remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/GLOWr")
remotes::install_github("ZWuLab/GLOWpipeline")

System Requirements

  • R >= 3.5.0
  • The Bioconductor package SeqArray (a hard dependency, for GDS/aGDS I/O)

Install the Bioconductor dependency with:

# install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("SeqArray")

Optional Dependencies

Several capabilities rely on Suggested packages installed on demand:

  • Coding-scan and aGDS paths: STAAR, gdsfmt, SNPRelate (Bioconductor).
  • Fast on-disk results IO: fst.

Quick Start

A genome-wide GLOW scan has three phases: chunk the genome, scan each chunk (typically one cluster-array task per chunk), then aggregate. The snippet below shows the call shapes for the first and last phases; the per-chunk scan (glow_scan_chunk() / run_scan_unit()) needs a GDS file plus a fitted null model and weight inputs, which a workflow script supplies (see the vignette).

library(GLOWpipeline)

# 1. Chunk the genome into sliding-window array tasks. Each row is one chunk:
#    a chromosome and a contiguous run of window start positions.
chrom_spans <- data.frame(
  chr   = c("21", "22"),
  start = c(5010000L, 10510000L),
  end   = c(48120000L, 50810000L)
)
chunks <- define_genome_chunks(
  chrom_spans,
  window_size = 2000, step_size = 1000,
  chunk_strategy = "fixed_mb", chunk_size_mb = 5
)
head(chunks)

# 2. Per chunk (one cluster-array task), run the scan over its windows.
#    glow_scan_chunk() / run_scan_unit() take a GDS path plus the resolved
#    null model + weight inputs from prepare_scan_run(); see the vignette.

# 3. Aggregate the per-chunk result files into a genome-wide table, flag
#    significant windows, and merge overlapping windows into loci.
# agg <- aggregate_scan_results(chunk_files, primary_test = "GLOW_Omni",
#                               alpha = 0.05)
# agg$scan_results_all   # genome-wide flat table
# agg$scan_sig_windows   # significant windows

For the full workflow (resolving the shared setup with prepare_scan_run(), running the scan, and aggregating), see the package vignette.

Zhang, H., Liu, M., Landers, J. E., and Wu, Z. (2026). Integrated weighted association test with application to genetic association studies. The Annals of Applied Statistics, 20(3), 2074-2097. https://doi.org/10.1214/26-AOAS2223

Related software / acknowledgments

GLOWpipeline builds on and interoperates with:

  • FAVOR — functional annotations underpinning the aGDS annotation paths consumed by the scan. Zhou, H., Arapoglou, T., Li, X., et al. (2023). FAVOR: functional annotation of variants online resource and annotator for variation across the human genome. Nucleic Acids Research, 51(D1), D1300-D1311. doi:10.1093/nar/gkac966
  • STAAR / STAARpipeline — the STAARpipeline analog this package mirrors; the coding aggregator merges native STAAR omnibi and uses STAARpipeline genes_info. Li, X., Li, Z., Zhou, H., et al. (2020). Dynamic incorporation of multiple in silico functional annotations empowers rare variant association analysis of large whole-genome sequencing studies at scale. Nature Genetics, 52, 969-983. doi:10.1038/s41588-020-0676-4. Li, Z., Li, X., Zhou, H., et al. (2022). A framework for detecting noncoding rare-variant associations of large-scale whole-genome sequencing studies. Nature Methods, 19, 1599-1611. doi:10.1038/s41592-022-01640-x
